question:
A moving-coil galvanometer has a rectangular coil of $N$ turns and area $A$ placed in a uniform radial magnetic field of flux density $B$. The moment of inertia of the coil about its axis is $I_{rot}$. The coil is shunted by a resistance $S$ to make an ammeter; the resistance of the galvanometer coil is $G$.

A very short current pulse passes through the ammeter terminals. The pulse duration is so small that the coil does not rotate appreciably during the pulse and damping can be neglected during the pulse. The angular impulse (time-integral of torque) imparted to the coil is measured to be $\Delta L$.

(i) Find the angular speed $\omega$ of the coil immediately after the pulse.
(ii) Find the total charge $Q$ that passed through the **ammeter terminals** during the pulse.
